slot.brief: Draw an alkene (figure, e.g., a cyclic diene) and ask for the dicarbonyl product(s) after ozonolysis with Zn/H2O; requires identifying both cleavage sites.

stem: The compound shown in the figure is subjected to ozonolysis followed by reductive work-up with Zn/H$_2$O. Which products are formed?

verdicts.working: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves both C=C bonds. Each cleavage opens the ring into two three-carbon fragments, each OHC–CH₂–CHO (propane-1,3-dial).

Independent check: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves both C=C bonds. Each cleavage opens the ring into two three-carbon fragments, each OHC–CH₂–CHO (propane-1,3-dial).
solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves both C=C bonds, converting each alkene carbon into a carbonyl group. Cleavage of the ring gives two identical three-carbon fragments:
$$\text{C}_1=\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3-\text{C}_4=\text{C}_5-\text{C}_6-\text{C}_1 \xrightarrow[\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} 2\,\text{OHC-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$$
Thus, two molecules of propane-1,3-dial are formed.
